assign.request: One coherent AI2 card page layout: chat as the right-hand column (a third at 1920/3440, footer at 390), exactly one chat scroll area with ext/Chat smart scroll, no white void, keep earlier fixes, remove dead CSS; prove with headless shots on the Dictate and ai-dashboard cards. Full ask: requirements.md.
steps: Read git status + diff of ai2/ and ext/Chat/
Measure the current card page headless (scroll areas, void)
Rewrite the card-page layout CSS as one rule set
Remove dead CSS from the competing edits
Prove: shots at 3440/1920 on Dictate + ai-dashboard, 390 on one; scroll-area count; console errors

log.msg: Read the uncommitted edits. Three competing layers: (1) chat-column-prompts put the chat in a right column under a CONTAINER query (.ai2-detail/.ai2-sub at 60em); (2) one-layout/columns-seams added grips and a separate --ai2-chat-sub token; (3) chat-ext-extract moved the chat into ext/Chat (chatbox-*), leaving .ai2-said-line and the old cost-table rules dead. Faces/markdown/done-checkbox/meter edits are content, not layout, and were kept untouched.

Measured before (1920, Dictate card with a sub-card open): the 60em container query failed the moment a sub-card halved the column, so BOTH card and sub-card fell back to footer chats: 4 scroll boxes in the work area (two .ai2-full, two .chatbox-log) and the sub-card's short body over ~400px of white. The chat logs also opened on their OLDEST lines: ext/Chat's smart scroll unlocked itself on first load.

decision.question: What decides whether the chat is a column or a footer?
options: the column's width (container query, what was there)
the window's width (media query at 40em, the same breakpoint as every other AI 2 phone rule)
decision.why: A sub-card opening shrinks the column, so a container query flips the chat to the bottom exactly when the owner opens something. The window does not change when a sub-card opens.

decision.question: With a sub-card open, which chat shows, and where?
options: each card keeps its own chat beside it (5 columns, the owner called it cramped)
one chat, the DEEPEST open card's, as the rightmost column; the parent's chat steps aside
decision.why: The owner: no narrow tall chat in between; one treatment for every card at any depth. Same assistant answers both, so nothing is lost. The layout is thirds: card | sub-card | chat.

decision.question: How wide is the chat by default?
options: clamp(22em, 33cqi, 64em) of the column (what was there)
a third of the room right of the rail: 33.333% of a top card's page, 50% of a sub-card's page (the sub column is 2fr)
decision.chose: a third of the room right of the rail, floor 18rem
decision.why: It is the same width with or without a sub-card open, so opening one moves nothing but the card. No container needed (a container on .ai2 would re-anchor the position:fixed selection flag).

decision.question: The sub-card seam's column also holds the chat. How does dragging it move only its two neighbours?
options: let the chat's default percentage follow the drag (moves three columns)
pin the chat at its current px width on the first drag move, for this session only

decision.question: Two chat width tokens (--ai2-chat and --ai2-chat-sub)?
decision.why: Only one chat column is ever on screen now, so it keeps its width as you move between a card and its sub-cards.

log.msg: Smart scroll fix (ext/Chat/Chat.js): only a scroll UP unlocks; a ResizeObserver re-pins the bottom when the box itself resizes. The old rule read at_bottom() on every scroll event, and our own jump's event arrived after the next batch of lines, so every card opened on its oldest line. Also Chat.css: a short conversation sits at the bottom of the log (first line margin-top auto), and the composer's max-height is gone (manager-new-card, for the owner).

CAVEAT, not mine to fix: ext/Chat/Mic.js line ~192 still sets the textarea's max-height inline (min(40vh, 12lh)) and overflow-y auto, deliberately, so a dictation over ~12 lines still scrolls inside the box. Mic.js belongs to the dictation manager; told manager-new-card. Nothing in the stylesheet fights it.

Dead CSS removed: .ai2-said-line, .ai2-cost th/td nowrap and .ai2-cost-sum (cost is group_faces now, no table), the 60em ai2-card container and its two @container blocks, .ai2-foot > .grip's container rule. Kept: Live card grid (its own), faces/meter/toc-done rules.

Proof (headless, zero console errors on every load). Scroll boxes with overflow that actually scroll: Dictate 3440 = rail + chat log; Dictate 1920 = rail + chat log; ai-dashboard 3440 and 1920 = rail + card body + chat log; 390 = card body + chat log (footer); sub-card open 1920 = rail + chat log. Exactly ONE chat scroller everywhere, pinned at the bottom (0px from bottom). Chat width: 919 of 2757px at 3440, 437 of 1313px at 1920 (a third of the room right of the rail). Gestures: wheel up froze (1500px from bottom, stayed put through a resize), wheel to bottom re-locked (0). Chat seam drag -150px: card 875 -> 729, chat 437 -> 583, rail unchanged; double-click reset to 437.

assign.outcome:
**Every AI 2 card now has one layout: the chat is the right-hand column, with one scroll area.**

On a wide screen a card shows card | chat, with the chat taking a third of the room. With a sub-card open it shows card | sub-card | chat, and the chat on screen is the deepest open card's. On a phone the chat is the footer. The chat no longer jumps to the bottom when a sub-card opens, it opens on the newest line, and each resize handle moves only the two columns beside it.
